# d3CRM — website enquiry CRM

> d3CRM connects website contact forms to a shared enquiry inbox for small teams and agencies. It includes an enquiry pipeline, assignments, follow-up dates, reply drafts, client workspaces, campaign reports, and CSV exports.

## Public product resources
- [Product overview](/): Website enquiry workflow for teams and agencies.
- [Features](/features): Implemented capabilities and workflow limits.
- [Interactive demo](/demo): Fictional, page-local workspace; no account required.
- [Guides](/guides): Public setup and lead management documentation.
- [Connect website forms](/guides/connect-website-forms): Field matching, origins, test mode, and live mode.
- [Manage client enquiries](/guides/manage-client-enquiries): Separate workspaces, roles, routing, and handover.
- [Follow up on website leads](/guides/follow-up-website-leads): Statuses, assignments, drafts, and the UTC agenda.
- [Free tools](/tools): Browser-only tools with no account requirement.
- [Campaign URL builder](/tools/campaign-url-builder): Create UTM-tagged links; does not install analytics.
- [Form launch checklist](/tools/form-launch-checklist): Review, copy, or print launch checks; does not inspect websites.

Reply drafts are reviewed and sent in the user's email app, not automatically sent by d3CRM. Follow-up dates use UTC. Campaign reports describe submitted enquiry context, not visitor analytics. Optional notifications, webhooks, and billing depend on deployment configuration. Do not infer pricing, certifications, customer counts, or capabilities absent from the public pages.

## Privacy and legal documents

- [Privacy Policy](/privacy): Actual account/workspace data flows, providers, retention, and privacy rights.
- [Terms of Service](/terms): Service agreement, customer responsibilities, subscriptions, and mandatory-rights protections.
- [Data Processing Agreement](/data-processing): Customer instructions and processor duties; restricted transfers need separately completed safeguards.
- [Account Data Notice](/account-data-notice): Specific account fields, purposes, consent withdrawal, and contact route.

Connected websites must publish the collecting business's own privacy notice and preserve any required consent. The d3CRM policy is not that business's collection notice. Keep optional marketing separate; do not assume that a generated form establishes a lawful processing ground. Do not import regulated international data until the required transfer arrangements are in place.

## Form integration guide for AI agents

Use the form-specific integration prompt from the d3CRM dashboard as the source of truth for the endpoint, schema, allowed origins, and publishable key. Never guess credentials or endpoints.

## Creating form definitions
Return JSON: {"name":"Contact form","schema":{"version":1,"fields":[{"id":"email","label":"Email address","type":"email","required":true}]}}
Names are 2–100 characters. Schemas contain 1–30 fields. Each field has a unique id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$, a label of 1–80 characters, type, and a boolean required value.
Types: text, email, tel, number, textarea, select, checkbox.
Select fields need 1–50 nonempty options. Optional maxLength is an integer from 1 to 10000.
Users import this JSON in Forms → New form → Build with AI, review it, and create the form. There is no public form-creation API; do not claim to have created a form by generating JSON.

## Website integration
POST JSON to the exact endpoint provided by the dashboard, /api/v1/forms/{slug}/submissions.
Headers: Content-Type: application/json and X-Form-Key: the publishable form key.
Send field IDs at the top level; do not wrap in data or schema. Numbers should be JSON numbers; checkboxes must be booleans. A required checkbox must be true. Omit blank optional fields. Add an off-screen, non-focusable _gotcha honeypot and send its value, normally empty.
The form must be Live. Requests from browsers must match the configured origin allowlist when set. The key is publishable and does not grant dashboard access. Keys are only shown on creation/rotation.

Optional campaign metadata goes in a separate top-level _context object: landing_page, referrer, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content. Do not put it in the form schema or nest answers inside it. URLs must use HTTP/HTTPS, have no credentials, and be at most 2048 characters; stored URLs exclude query strings and fragments. UTM values are strings of at most 200 characters. Read campaign parameters from the current URL using URLSearchParams; omit missing values. Prefer location.origin + location.pathname for landing_page. Do not add cookies or storage tracking. Do not send personal data in URLs or campaign values. Invalid _context returns 422 with fields._context. Existing integrations may omit it. Metadata is included in webhook events and _context.* CSV columns.

Owners/admins have a Connect website wizard that generates HTML/JavaScript or a handler for an existing form element ID. In test mode, POST the same payload/key to /api/v1/forms/{slug}/verify instead of /submissions. HTTP 200 with {ok:true,test:true,schemaVersion} means a valid dry run: no enquiry, quota usage, assignment, email, or webhook is created. It checks the same live form/key/origin and schema rules and records an endpoint-check event. Test code must run on the actual website to exercise its browser CORS policy. Replace the test handler with one live handler, do not attach both. A dashboard endpoint check does not prove the website is installed or that email delivery works. Only send live test enquiries with user approval.

## Responses and UX
201: {ok:true,submission:{id,createdAt}}. 202: accepted.
422: {error,fields}; fields maps IDs to validation errors.
401: missing/invalid key. 403: disallowed origin. 404: missing/inactive form or incorrect key. 413: body too large (64 KB limit). 429: rate limited.
Use accessible labels, field errors, a loading state, duplicate-submit protection, success feedback, and network-error handling. Preserve user input when submission fails. Do not send test leads without user approval.
